title: Iberia Airlines 602
summary: Iberia Flight 602 descended below safe altitude while approaching Ibiza Airport. The captain and first officer were discussing a football match with the tower controller and failed to notice the dangerous descent rate. The aircraft struck Mount Atalayasa 90 feet below its 1,515-foot summit, killing all 104 people on board.
probable_cause: The pilot failed to maintain the minimum flight altitude for a visual approach to Runway 07.

title: JAT 367
summary: JAT Flight 367, a DC-9 en route from Copenhagen to Belgrade, was destroyed by an explosion in the baggage compartment at 4:01 p.m. The investigation concluded that a bomb had been placed in checked baggage. A man suspected of placing the bomb checked in luggage in Stockholm but did not reboard when the aircraft departed Copenhagen. Only one flight attendant, Vesna Vulovic, survived the crash, the sole survivor of the 28 on board.

title: Sterling Airways 296
summary: Sterling Airways Flight 296, a Caravelle, crashed into a mountain ridge on approach to Dubai on March 14, 1972. The investigation found that the crew descended below the minimum prescribed altitude due to incorrect information from an outdated flight plan and misreading of the weather radar, which led them to believe they were closer to Dubai than they actually were.
probable_cause: The pilots descended below minimum prescribed altitude during approach. This was attributed to incorrect information on the outdated flight plan and/or misreading of the weather radar which gave the pilots false impression of their proximity to the destination airport.

title: Japan Airlines 471
summary: Japan Air Lines Flight 471 crashed short of New Delhi airport. The flight took off from Bangkok at 11:21 UTC and was cleared for a straight-in ILS approach to runway 28 at 14:43 UTC. The plane crashed into the banks of the Yamuna River shortly after the 23-mile DME report. Investigators disagreed: Japanese investigators pointed to a false glide path signal, while Indian investigators blamed pilot error for ignoring instruments without runway visual contact.

title: Cathay Pacific 700Z bombing
summary: Cathay Pacific Flight 700Z, a Convair CV-880, crashed 30 miles southeast of Pleiku on 15 June 1972, killing all 81 occupants. Flight data recorder showed the aircraft flying at 29,000 feet on course until 05:59 GMT when recorded data became nonsensical for 30 seconds before stopping. Investigation determined an explosive device in the passenger cabin caused structural failure and loss of control at cruising altitude.
probable_cause: Explosive device likely located within the passenger cabin.

factors.evidence: An inquiry determined the crash was caused by an explosive device, likely located within the passenger cabin.

title: British European Airways 548
summary: Hawker Siddeley Trident entered a deep stall during initial climb shortly after takeoff from Heathrow and descended steeply until crashing near Staines. The aircraft had not achieved sufficient airspeed and high-lift devices were not properly configured for the climb phase. The public inquiry principally blamed the captain for failing to maintain airspeed and configure the aircraft correctly. The captain had an undiagnosed heart condition and the co-pilot had limited experience. The aircraft's T-tail design and high-lift system made it vulnerable to deep stall if airspeed was insufficient and high-lift devices were not extended.
probable_cause: The captain failed to maintain sufficient airspeed and failed to extend high-lift devices properly during initial climb, causing the aircraft to enter a deep stall from which recovery was impossible. The captain's undiagnosed heart condition may have contributed to impaired judgment. An unspecified technical problem apparently resolved before takeoff and limited co-pilot experience with the aircraft also contributed to the accident.

factors.evidence: Captain failed to maintain airspeed and configure high-lift devices correctly for climbing phase.

Co-pilot had limited experience and was not qualified as pilot-flying for the aircraft.

Aircraft crashed into ground near Staines-upon-Thames narrowly missing busy main road.

title: Interflug 450
summary: Interflug Flight 450 with 156 aboard took off from Berlin-Schönefeld at 16:30. At 16:43, thirteen minutes into flight at 8900 m altitude, the crew reported problems with elevators and was approximately 10 degrees off course. At 16:51 the crew began fuel dump. Flight attendants reported smoke in the rear section of the cabin. At 16:59:25 the crew issued a mayday indicating problems controlling altitude. Seconds later the tail section, weakened by fire, separated causing uncontrolled descent and in-flight breakup. Fire started from hot-air tube leak at 300°C that damaged electrical insulation causing short circuits.
probable_cause: In-flight fire in cargo bay caused by hot-air tube leak, leading to electrical short circuits and structural failure of the tail section.

title: Aeroflot 217
summary: Aeroflot Flight 217 was flying at 1200 m when ATC cleared descent to 400 m. The crew confirmed and started to descend normally, but the aircraft failed to level off and passed the 400 m mark at 20 m/s descent rate with engines at low thrust. The aircraft crashed with landing gear up and spoilers retracted. Investigators concluded that the probable cause was psycho-physiological incapacitation of the crew.

title: 1972 Andes flight disaster
summary: A Fairchild FH-227D carrying 45 members of a Uruguayan rugby team and their relatives crashed in the Andes Mountains on 13 October 1972, killing 31 occupants. The inexperienced co-pilot Dante Lagurara, while being trained by experienced Captain Ferradas, mistakenly believed the aircraft had passed the Curicó turning point when it was still 37 kilometers east of that position. The crew initiated descent prematurely in instrument meteorological conditions with cloud cover obscuring the terrain, causing the aircraft to strike a mountain ridge at 12,020 feet, shearing off both wings and the tail cone.
probable_cause: Navigation error by the co-pilot who misjudged the aircraft position while in cloud, leading to premature descent and collision with mountainous terrain.

title: Braathens SAFE 239
summary: The Fokker F28 crashed during approach to Oslo after the pilots took a shortcut and turned too early due to ILS system deviations. Combined with false signals from the instrument landing system and confusion about their position, the aircraft descended below safe altitude and struck terrain near Asker. The investigation found navigational error was the probable cause, with the ILS known to deviate up to twenty-five degrees under certain conditions.

title: Eastern Air Lines 401
summary: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 crashed in the Florida Everglades shortly before midnight after the autopilot inadvertently disconnected. A subtle bump of the yoke switched the autopilot from altitude hold to Control Wheel Steering mode. While the crew was focused on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light, they did not notice the autopilot disconnection and the aircraft gradually lost altitude until striking the ground.
probable_cause: A subtle bump of the yoke caused the autopilot to switch from altitude hold mode to Control Wheel Steering mode. The crew's focus on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light distracted them from noticing the altitude loss.
